items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude the resident pair from worker-workspace checks**

The filter matches every workspace whose label merely starts with the repository basename. Full mode creates the normal resident pair with the label `<repo> agents` (`executable_herdr-agents:2071`), which this selects even though the new Stop checklist says that pair stays resident. Thus `make check-regime-boundary` fails, and `make validate-agent-assets` emits a warning, in the normal healthy full-mode state; match the `<repo> worker ` label prefix instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: not-applicable:the filter prefix is "<main checkout basename> worker " (scripts/check-regime-boundary.sh), so the resident "<repo> agents" workspace does not match; verified in the diff

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Correlate PONGs with the linkage PING**

A PONG is considered successful solely by team, sender, recipient, and the fixed `task_id=bringup`, so a PONG left by an earlier worker instance satisfies this immediately. This occurs after a worker is removed and re-added with a reused `-aNNN` identity; message history is deliberately retained (`SKILL.md:35`). The command can therefore print `pong=yes` for a new worker that never answered this PING, allowing the documented PONG-before-task gate to be bypassed. Restrict the lookup to messages created after, or otherwise linked to, this invocation's PING.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:b91f949

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the linkage PONG wait before arithmetic**

When `HERDR_AGENTS_LINKAGE_PONG_WAIT` is set to a nonnumeric value such as `foo` or an invalid arithmetic expression such as `1/0`, this expansion aborts the `set -u` shell after `agmsg-dispatch` has already read the PING. `--add-worker` then exits without printing its required final `linkage=` evidence line, making a configuration typo look like an unexplained worker-launch failure; reject invalid values before computing the deadline.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:00573f3

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject ambiguous orchestrator identities before linkage**

When the selected team has multiple non-`-aNNN` Claude identities and the worker identity already exists, `ensure_worker_identity` does not perform its normal uniqueness check and this pipeline silently selects the first sorted name. The PING and PONG can then be routed through a stale or different orchestrator identity while `--add-worker` reports `pong=yes`, even though the active orchestrator did not receive the response; reject multiple leaders here instead of using `head -n 1`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:00573f3

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Correlate linkage PONGs with the current PING**

When an old worker's response to an earlier, identical `task_id=bringup` PING is delayed until after this invocation inserts its new PING (for example, around removal and re-addition of a reused `-aNNN` identity), this query reports `pong=yes` even if the new worker never received the new PING. Fresh evidence: the `id > ${ping_id}` filter now rejects PONGs already in history, but it still accepts a delayed response written after the new PING; include a per-invocation nonce or an explicit reply-to identifier in the PONG before reporting the documented gate as satisfied.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:9e36e63

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Flag missing identities for active worker seats**

When an active pair or worker worktree has lost its only registration, `identities.sh` yields no rows, this assigns `names=0`, and the check reports no violation. The new Stop checklist requires exactly one identity for each active checkout, so `make check-regime-boundary` can pass while delivery has no identity to target; distinguish inactive agent types from active seats and flag zero names for the latter.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scan all worktrees for untracked orchestration files**

When the orchestrator runs this check from the main checkout while an additional worker worktree still contains an untracked `.orchestration/...` artifact, this command inspects only `root`, not the paths already enumerated by `git worktree list`. The new boundary check therefore exits successfully despite the required zero-untracked-tail condition being violated in the worker checkout; run the untracked-file probe for each registered worktree.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify placement panes belong to the new workspace**

After a failed or retried spawn, a retained placement record can name a live pane in an older workspace. This path always prefers that record without checking its `<workspace>:<pane>` value against `workspace_id`; `agmsg-dispatch` then resolves pane IDs globally, so the old worker can read the PING and make `--add-worker` report `linkage=ok` even though the newly created worker was never reached. Reject placement records for a different workspace and fall back to the new pane lookup.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:9e36e63

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Constrain worker-workspace checks to matching pane CWD**

When two independent checkouts share a basename (for example, two separate `dotfiles` clones) and the other checkout has a `dotfiles worker <name>` workspace open, this label-prefix filter reports it as an additional worker for the current repository and makes its boundary check fail. `find_managed_workspaces` in `executable_herdr-agents` already resolves this ambiguity by checking the workspace panes' `cwd`; apply the same repository-path check here rather than relying on the non-unique label.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:2721f0c

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject mixed runtime identities on an active seat**

When the configured worker worktree has one `claude-code` identity and one `codex` identity (or the main checkout has its required Claude identity plus a Codex identity), each per-type count is one and this check reports no violation. That leaves two physical identities registered at one active checkout despite the Stop checklist's exactly-one-seat requirement, allowing stale identities to survive the boundary check and later make worker routing ambiguous; count identities across both runtime types for active seats.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:d806a3d

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate placement panes before using them for linkage**

If a failed or retried spawn leaves a placement record for an exited pane in the same workspace, the workspace-ID check accepts that record and dispatches to the old pane instead of the newly spawned pane. `agmsg-dispatch` rejects a pane that is no longer listed, so `--add-worker` reports `linkage=unreached` and exits even though the current worker pane is available. Fresh evidence: the new check excludes only records from a different workspace, not stale panes within the current workspace; verify the recorded pane is still present before preferring it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:d806a3d

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Check the main checkout's orchestrator lock**

When this target runs from a linked worktree, `root` is that worker checkout while `main` correctly resolves to the main checkout. Passing `root` here makes `orchestrator_seat_lock_warnings` look for a non-worker Claude identity and live Claude process in the worker checkout, so it returns no warning and misses a bare orchestrator lock at the main checkout; pass `main` to the helper while retaining `root` only to locate the module.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:d806a3d

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject placement records from before this spawn**

After a failed/retried spawn, a retained record can name an older pane that is still listed in the same workspace but has no live agent, while this invocation creates a new worker pane. This membership-only check accepts the old record, so `agmsg-dispatch` targets it and reports `linkage=unreached` even though the fresh worker is reachable. Fresh evidence: the code receives the pre-spawn pane set in `known` but never rejects a placement pane contained in it; treat such records as stale and fall back to the post-spawn pane lookup.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Direct pane-less bring-up through agmsg-dispatch**

For the pane-less cases this new checklist explicitly incorporates (plain shell, mosh/SSH), “exactly as that bullet describes” still directs the operator to send the PING with `poke.sh` (line 22). In an unviewed/headless Herdr workspace, the newly added guidance says that command exits 14/15 rather than waking the worker, so the mandated PONG-before-task gate cannot complete. Update this checklist/bullet to use `agmsg-dispatch` and its receipt/PONG evidence in that case.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve linkage diagnostics when dispatch fails**

When `agmsg-dispatch` cannot get a read receipt, this redirects away both its output and the exact PING invocation, then emits only `linkage=unreached rc=… hint=…`. The newly added blocker procedure requires the exact command and `read_at`/PONG query as attached evidence after trying this wake path; because the pane ID and per-invocation task ID are not printed, the operator cannot reconstruct or report that evidence from the required final line. Emit the invocation and the applicable receipt/PONG query (or its unavailability) to stderr before returning.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.body:
The following taps are not trusted:
  aws/tap
  azure/bicep
  hashicorp/tap

Homebrew is currently ignoring formulae, casks and commands from these taps because tap trust is required.

Prefer trusting only the specific formulae, casks or commands you need.
Trust installed formulae from these taps with:
  brew trust --formula azure/bicep/bicep
  brew trust --formula hashicorp/tap/packer
Trust other specific casks and commands with:
  brew trust --cask <user>/<tap>/<cask>
  brew trust --command <user>/<tap>/<command>
Whole-tap trust is broader and includes all current and future formulae,
casks and commands from the listed taps. Trust whole taps with:
  brew trust aws/tap azure/bicep hashicorp/tap
Untap them with:
  brew untap aws/tap azure/bicep hashicorp/tap
To disable trust checks:
  export HOMEBREW_NO_REQUIRE_TAP_TRUST=1
This is not recommended and will be removed in a later release.
For more information, see:
  https://docs.brew.sh/Tap-Trust
